sections.content: The Schipperke, known for its energy and intelligence, is a small breed with a big personality. These dogs are famous for their lively nature and strong bond with their owners. In this detailed guide, we’ll explore the history, temperament, care, training, and health of the breed to help you determine if this delightful dog is right for you.

sections.section: History and Origin of the Schipperke
sections.content: The Schipperke originates from Belgium, where the breed was developed by canal boat captains to act as watchdogs. Their name, which means “little captain” in Flemish, reflects their working history on the waterways. The breed was recognized by the American Kennel Club (AKC) in 1904.

AKC Height: 10-13 inches AKC Height: 10-13 inches AKC Weight: 10-18 pounds AKC Weight: 10-18 pounds Colors: Black Colors: Black Life Expectancy: 12-15 years Life Expectancy: 12-15 years Group: Non-Sporting Group Group: Non-Sporting Group
This is a small, sturdy breed with a distinctive fox-like face and a dense, black coat. Their pricked ears and alert expression make them stand out among other small breeds.

sections.section: Is the Schipperke the Right Dog for You
sections.content: This dog is an excellent choice for owners who appreciate an energetic, intelligent, and loyal companion. However, their unique temperament and care needs mean they are not the best fit for everyone.
